title: What is VPN and How it Works?
author: Achyuth KP
description:
Everything you need to know about VPN: What it is? What does it actually provide? How it Works?

Almost all internet users have heard or even used a VPN or Virtual Private Network before. A VPN is a connection method used to add security and privacy to private and public networks. VPN is used for hiding our IP address so we can surf pseudo-anonymously, it is not like no one will know about your IP address as you turn on the VPN as the VPN provider will know your original IP address. VPN provider will replace your unique IP address with a random IP address.

A VPN will protect the data you are transferring over a public WIFI. Corporate companies use VPN to protect sensitive data. This is the main reason corporation are using VPN. Usage of a VPN is increasing and becoming more popular. VPN provider can change the gateway city, for example, if you live in Bengaluru, with the VPN you will be appearing to live in San Francisco, New York, a city you love the most. User can choose the country he/she likes for their internet connection. Using a VPN will result in a different gateway with a different IP address.

The most fun fact is you can access the government blocked websites with VPN. VPNs are having advanced encryption protocols and secure tunneling techniques to encapsulate all online data transfers, no data will be lost or even connection cannot be hijacked. You only understood the benefits of VPN usage. There are still plenty of internet users who don’t know about VPN.

The history of VPN technology and services, VPN starts in 1996, when a google developer Gurdeep Singh-pall started developing the Peer to Peer Tunneling Protocol (PPTP). VPN technology was originally developed only enormous companies and organization for their own goals, and it wasn’t meant for casual internet users. Companies needed a secure and private method to make communication and transfer and allow employees to access important files remotely without there being any risk of unauthorized users hijack the sensitive data. As time passed, more powerful encryption standards started being implemented to further secure business communication.

Let us know how the VPN works now. The user should download the application/software provided by VPN Provider. After downloading the user must turn on the VPN, a connection will be established. After the connection is established, an encrypted tunnel is created between the user and the VPN provider. You can select any gateway provided by VPN whatever request you send to VPN provider will be encrypted, VPN provider will decrypt your request and facilities will be provided to the user.

There are many advantages and disadvantages of using a VPN.

Advantages of VPN:

  1. A VPN hides your IP address.
  2. VPN helps you bypass Geo-pass.
  3. VPN helps you secure your online connection.
  4. A VPN can bypass the firewall.
  5. A VPN can prevent bandwidth throttling.
  6. A VPN offers secure torrent.
  7. VPN makes online gaming better.
  8. VPN might help you avoid online discrimination.
  9. Gain at least some anonymity online by hiding your true location.
  10. Protect yourself from snooping on untrustworthy Wi-Fi hotspots.

Disadvantages of VPN

  1. VPNs can sometimes slow down your online speed
  2. Using the wrong VPN can put your privacy in danger.
  3. Quality VPNs will cost more money.
  4. Not all devices support VPNs.

Use a good VPN to secure your private data. VPN is the perfect choice to secure your online data transfer and freely access blocked content. Look for a VPN provider who provides high-speed connection, fast VPN protocols and unlimited bandwidth.

VPN types:

  1. Standalone VPN services.
  2. Bowser extensions.
  3. Router VPN.
  4. Corporate VPN.

Best VPNs servers are:

  1. NordVPN — #1 VPN in 2020
  2. ExpressVPN — #1 for speed
  3. CyberGhost — Best VPN for beginners
  4. Surfshark — Best budget-friendly VPN
  5. PrivateVPN — Best protocol variety
  6. Proton VPN — Best free VPN

Approximately 1.79 billion internet users use a VPN on a daily basis. The number will grow up drastically in the future. VPNs become more and more common in the next years. The evolution of the Internet brought about the new amazing development, but also exposed online users to Internet censorship, hacker threats, data mining, and getting spammed with ads. All of that helped the young VPN market grow as more and more people realized using VPNs was one of the only things they could do to protect their privacy on the Internet.

title: What is the difference between Virtual Reality, Augmented Reality, and Mixed Reality?
author: Achyuth KP
description:
How Virtual Reality, Augmented Reality, and Mixed Reality are Changing the World?

There is rapid growth in the field of Virtual Reality, Augmented reality, and Mixed reality. You might have confusion with these different technologies, these technologies integrate virtual and real-world elements and also have similarities.

Virtual Reality (VR): An experience where a user leaves the real-world environment behind and enters into an entirely virtual environment via a VR headset.

Augmented Reality (AR): An experience where virtual objects are being imposed into a real-world environment via smartphones, AR glasses, tablets, and a heads up display.

Mixed Reality (MR): Mixed Reality is a step beyond augmented reality, where the virtual objects placed in the real world can be interacted with and respond as if they are real objects. We can say Mixed Reality is like Augmented reality, Version 2.0.

Still not clear? Let’s go deeper into the details.

Virtual Reality

Virtual Reality is a three-dimensional computer-generated environment that can be explored and interacted with by a person. This technology immerses users in a completely virtual environment; the most advanced VR experiences, even provide freedom of movement, and users can move in a digital environment and hear sounds. Moreover, individual hand controllers can be used to enhance VR experiences. The person needs to wear a special VR headset to experience Virtual Reality. Usually, a smartphone will be inserted into a VR headset.

I think everyone has noticed a small cardboard icon on YouTube, this enables a 360-degree mode, where you can wear a VR headset and watch it. I suggest you, people, not to watch any horror videos or movies or even play Horror games you will freak out.

This VR headset makes a person believe they are moving among virtual objects on the screen. Virtual Reality tool helps the surgeons plan the surgery, and A person can feel the place before he/she travels to the destination, Pilots can be trained with the help of virtual reality. Soldiers can be prepared for combat scenarios, but the future will be full of even more VR applications as businesses of all kinds figure out ways the technology can enhance operations.

The smartphone comes into place while using google cardboard, Samsung Gear VR, and Google Daydream. VR headset is also connected to a PC or Console to simulate the person’s physical presence in virtual reality.

Augmented Reality

Augmented Reality overlays virtual objects in the real-world environment. In augmented reality, users can see ad interact with the real world while the digital content will be added to it.

The best example of augmented reality is Pokemon Go. Millions of people, including me, have been rushing with their smartphones in search of the new Pokemon creature. In India, many of them used to download the game through other websites as it wasn’t officially released in India (Google Play-store).

Augmented Reality is a system that fulfills three essential features. They are a combination of real and virtual worlds, real-time interactions, and accurate 3D registration of virtual and real objects. The virtual objects have sensors with information, and it might be constructive or destructive.

Augmented Reality alters one’s perceptional of the real-world environment, whereas virtual reality completely replaces the user’s real-world environment with a simulated one.

Any smartphones can support many AR experiences. An example of AR is ARkit by Apple and ARCore by Google. AR is useful for more than just entertainment. Walmart built an AR application, as the person faces the camera to any product present in the mart, it will display the details of the product and its price. AR technology can enhance the travelling experience in many ways. Imagine you went to another country and you can’t read the road signs, all you need is to download the application and face the camera towards the sign. An example of this application is the Google lens.

Go to the google play store or Apple store, and you can easily download an AR app and try this technology. There’s a different way to experience augmented reality, though with special AR headsets, such as Google Glass, where digital content is displayed on a tiny screen in front of a user’s eye.

Mixed Reality

Mixed Reality is the most recent development in reality technologies. There are two forms of Mixed Reality. Mixed Reality starts with the real world and Mixed Reality that starts with the virtual world. Real-world is not just overlaid, but the person can interact with it. Virtual content is added to it. In Virtual Worlds, the whole environment is replaced by the digital environment, and the real-world will be blocked. It sounds the same as Virtual Reality, but digital objects will overlap the real-world. Wherein VR, it will not be connected with the real-world at all. To experience Mixed Reality, you can wear Windows Mixed Reality Headsets. Mixed Reality is stepping beyond Augmented Reality because users can interact in real-time with digital objects that are placed within the real-world.

Mixed Reality headsets offer a holographic experience through translucent glasses. Example of Mixed Reality is Microsoft’s HoloLens, Samsung Odyssey, Lenovo Explorer, Acer Windows Mixed reality. It is a gesture or voice recognition technology through the MR headset that helps deliver a believable Mixed Reality. Mixed reality, not just overlays, but anchors digital objects into the real world. Mixed Reality is way more step beyond Virtual Reality and Augmented Reality.

You might have heard Heads-up display in costly cars, earlier only speed of the car was displayed, now the whole thing as changed. Heads up display now show the route direction, the speed limit.

What is the difference between Virtual Reality, Augmented Reality, and Mixed Reality? was originally published in The Narrow World on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.

title: What is Artificial Intelligence?
author: Achyuth KP
description:
Understanding Artificial Intelligence and future of AI

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is the ability of a machine or a computer system to copy the human intelligence process, learn from experience, adapt to new information and perform human-like activities. Discussions of artificial intelligence (AI) have created a certain amount of unease by those who fear it will quickly evolve from being a benefit to human society to taking over.

The field of AI wasn’t formally founded until 1956, at a conference at Dartmouth College, in Hanover, New Hampshire, where the term artificial intelligence was first coined.

John McCarthy is one of the “founding fathers” of artificial intelligence, together with Alan Turing, Marvin Minsky, Allen Newell, and Herbert A. Simon. McCarthy coined the term “artificial intelligence” in 1955 and organized the famous Dartmouth Conference in Summer 1956. This conference started AI as a field. John McCarthy was an American computer scientist and cognitive scientist. He spent most of his career at Stanford University.

Artificial Intelligence has received a lot of focus and attention in the last couple of years. It is getting a lot of attention from investors, these days and with good reason. It’s a technology with the potential to transform everything from transportation to cloud computing. There has been a boom in the innovations that have artificial intelligence at its base. Obviously, the internet has played a crucial role in the development of artificial intelligence-enabled services.

Norvig and Russell gave four different approaches that have historically defined the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI):

  1. Thinking humanly
  2. Acting humanly
  3. Thinking rationally
  4. Acting rationally

Artificial Intelligence is a technology that can improve the world for the better, but Artificial Intelligence is programmed to do something devastating: Autonomous weapons are artificial intelligence systems that are programmed to kill. If this technology fell in the hands of the wrong person these weapons can easily cause mass damage. To avoid threatened by the wrong person, these weapons should be designed with a self destruct switch.

The is Artificial Intelligence is designed to do something beneficial, but it develops a destructive method for achieving its goal. This can happen whenever the programmer fails to design in a proper way with perfect protocols. Example of this failure while designing: If you tell a self-driving car to take you to the airport as fast as possible, it might get you there chased by the police and helicopters and it does what you haven’t wanted but literally does what you asked for.

Stephen Hawking, Elon Musk, Steve Wozniak, Bill Gates, and many other big names in science and technology have recently expressed concern in the media and via open letters about the risks posed by AI, joined by many leading AI researchers. They stated, Superhuman Artificial Intelligence could provide incalculable benefits, but could also end the human race if deployed incautiously.

Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk made the statement, AI is a fundamental risk to the existence of human civilization. He tweeted that he fears a global arms race for Artificial Intelligence will cause the third World War.

Artificial Intelligence helps in many different ways Self-driving cars helps in the prevention of many road accidents. If a tourist visited a country and he/she is not familiar with the language, artificial intelligence helps a lot. Self-driving cars and computers that play chess are two examples of machines with artificial intelligence. In addition, a variety of industries have begun using AI to improve their work processes, such as healthcare, manufacturing, banking and retail. In addition, AI is finding multiple beneficial uses in cybersecurity.
AI is a wide field of study incorporating various technologies, methods, and theories that focus on combining large amounts of data with defined rules and fast, repetitive processing. This enables the software to advance and improve its ability to complete tasks by recognizing patterns and features in the data sets.

AI programming focuses on three cognitive skills: learning, reasoning, and self-correction.

Learning processes: This aspect focuses on acquiring data and creating rules for how to turn the data into actionable information. The rules, which are called algorithms, provide computing devices with step-by-step instructions for how to complete a specific task.

Reasoning processes: This aspect focuses on choosing the right algorithm to reach the desired outcome.

Self-correction processes: This aspect is designed to continually fine-tune algorithms and ensure they provide the most accurate results possible.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is a young discipline of sixty years, which is a set of sciences, theories and techniques (including mathematical logic, statistics, probabilities, computational neurology, computer science) that aims to imitate the cognitive abilities of a human being.

Interesting technologies of Artificial intelligence are, Natural Language Generation, Speech Recognition, Machine Learning Platforms, Virtual Agents, Decision Management, AI Optimized Hardware, Deep Learning Platforms, Robotic Process Automation, Text Analytics and Natural Language Processing (NLP), Biometrics, Cyber Defense, Content Creation, Emotion Recognition, Image Recognition, Marketing Automation.

Sony created a robotic dog called Aibo, one of its first toys that could be bought and played with. It could express emotions and could also recognize its owner. This was the first of its kind, however, today you will find more expensive and evolved versions of the same.

Artificial intelligence (AI) makes it possible for machines to learn from experience, adjust to new inputs and perform human-like tasks. Using the technologies, computers can be trained to accomplish specific tasks by processing large amounts of data and recognizing patterns in the data. AI automates repetitive learning and discovery through data. But AI is different from hardware-driven, robotic automation. Instead of automating manual tasks, AI performs frequent, high-volume, computerized tasks reliably and without fatigue. For this type of automation, human inquiry is still essential to set up the system and ask the right questions.

Artificial Intelligence is going to change every industry, but we have to understand the limits. The principle limitation of artificial intelligence is that it learns from the data. There is no other way in which knowledge can be incorporated. Today’s artificial intelligence systems are trained to do a clearly defined task. The system that plays poker cannot play solitaire or chess. The system that detects fraud cannot drive a car or give you legal advice. In fact, an AI system that detects health care fraud cannot accurately detect tax fraud or warranty claims fraud. How cool it is that the AI system will turn on the AC in your house as soon as you leave your office and the car self-drives you to your home so that you can relax for some time.

title: What are the different types of Artificial Intelligence?
author: Achyuth KP
description:
Impressive Artificial Intelligence: Definition, Subsets, Types, future of AI

Everyone has heard the term Artificial Intelligence and many people are still having confusion between Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Deep Learning and Data Science.

Machine Learning and Deep Learning are a subset of Artificial Intelligence. Data science has an intersection with artificial intelligence, but it is not a subset of artificial intelligence and Data Science is all about data.

Artificial Intelligence is a program that can sense, reason, act and adapt. Machine Learning is an Algorithm whose performance improves as they are exposed to more data over time. Deep Learning is Subset of Machine Learning in which multilayered neural networks learn from the vast amount of data. AI has been growing exponentially, in the past decade, it is already been touching our lives in many ways.

It will be tough to learn and code AI program in the beginning. You will get confused with the code, once you understand completely it will be easy for you. I guarantee you one thing, it will be more interesting after you come to know how to write AI programs. There are two programming languages, where you can write code easily compared to other programming languages as these programming languages are having many inbuilt functions.

Programming languages are Python and R. I guess everyone is familiar with Python and many of them won’t be known about R language. Yeah, we can code an AI program both in Python and R. Python is the leading programming language in 2020. As the scope of AI is increasing day by day, even Python Programming language value is increasing, as it is easy to write AI code using python.

Artificial Intelligence is classified into four types based on their functionality.

Four types of Artificial Intelligence:

  1. Reactive machine AI.
  2. Limited Memory AI.
  3. Theory of mind AI.
  4. Self-aware AI.

REACTIVE MACHINE AI:

Reactive Machine AI includes machines that operate based on the present data, by taking into account only the current situation. They neither have the ability to form memories nor to use past experiences to inform current decisions. Reactive AI Machines cannot form an inference from a data to evaluate their future actions.

The best example of Reactive Machine AI is Deep Blue, an IBM chess program which beats the world champion Garry Kasparov (in 1997) is one of the most impressive AI Machine built so far. It is the first chess AI program.

Similar to this Google’s AlphaGo, which has beaten top human Go (It’s a game) experts, can’t evaluate all potential future moves either. They can perform a narrowed range of predefined tasks.

LIMITED MEMORY AI:

Limited Memory AI can make informed decisions by studying the past data from its memory. Such an AI has a short-lived or temporary memory that can be used to store past experiences and hence evaluate future actions.

The Best example for Limited Memory AI is Self driving Cars, uses the data collected in the recent past to make immediate decisions. Self driving cars uses sensors to identify civilians that are crossing the road, which also include lane markings, traffic lights, curves in the road, Senses the speed limit and adapts it. They use this to make better driving decisions and helps in preventing future accidents.

THEORY OF MIND AI:

The Theory of Mind AI is more advanced type of Artificial intelligence it will focus mainly on emotional intelligence so that human beliefs and thoughts can be better comprehended.

Theory of mind is all about understanding the creatures, objects and human behavior, their actions, thoughts, attitude, sentimental thoughts and emotions that affect their own behavior.

Theory of Mind AI is speculated to play a major role in human psychology. It is not completely developed yet, but regress research is happening in this area.

SELF-AWARE AI:

Moving on to the last type of Artificial Intelligence that is self-aware AI includes machines that have their own consciousness and become self-aware. This type of AI does not exist yet. It is far fare, but in the future achieving this is possible. Let us pray that we don’t reach this state of AI.

Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk made the statement, AI is a fundamental risk to the existence of human civilization. He tweeted that he fears a global arms race for Artificial Intelligence will cause the third World War.

Even the physicist Stephen Hawking stated, Superhuman Artificial Intelligence could provide incalculable benefits, but could also end the human race if deployed incautiously.
